examples.name: Default
examples.summary: An overview's usage strip: four StatTiles in one card, split by dividers, each delta aligned to the end of its cell. One cell per row in a narrow box, two from the group's medium size, all four in a row on a wide one.

examples.name: BesideCard
examples.summary: A dashboard row: the usage strip beside a taller card. The row stretches the group to the card's height and the cells share it, so no empty band sits under the tiles.

examples.name: MissingData
examples.summary: A row where some cells have no history. A cell with no trend draws the same gray placeholder curve as soon as a sibling draws a sparkline, so every label and figure stays on one line: Not enough data when the value is there, No data when it is missing, Couldn't load when the request failed.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same data written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<StatTileGroup>` tag with `<StatTile label value unit delta />` tags inside into a real `StatTileGroup` of `StatTile`s. The attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry.

examples.name: Page JSON
examples.summary: The same data in the marketing site's page JSON: `StatTileGroup` is a scene and its tiles are the scene's `children` (each a `StatTile` scene with its own `props`). A band places it by name in its `scene` slot (here `console-showcase-section` with `variant: "diagram"`) and `SitePage` renders the entry with no code.
